featured_reviews.name: Aaisha Kodapanakkal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yesterday (22 december 2025) I had an appointment with Dr. Amit Mishra at 8pm.
I reached Satya hospital at 7.30ish since I came directly after work. So I was aware that I would have to wait until 8pm at least.
At first, I waited until 8.20pm (which is already a little late for my 8pm appointment) and asked the receptionist how long would it take? She said that there was another patient before me who still had to go and then it would be my turn.
I waited and waited and then at 9.15pm she tells me that I could visit now!!! When I go upstairs I see 5 other people standing there.. and confirm from the nurse if they're waiting in line. She says yes there are 3 or 4 patients to be attended to before my turn.
I wonder how long more it would have taken because I informed the receptionist to cancel my appointment and walked out of the hospital!
The whole idea of taking appointments is so that people are aware of the time they have to be there at. It's very disrespectful to keep people waiting without giving any valid reason. I would have understood if there was any emergency that was being attended to but again it should be communicated properly. Please make sure to have a better organization system or don't take too many patients if you can't handle it time wise.. Or just cancel the whole appointment format and keep it walk in! I'm really very disappointed and frustrated with my first time experience here to have waited for almost 1 hour 15 mins (only including time since appointment time schedule)

(Also posted at Dr. Amit Mishra Ortho Care Clinic)

featured_reviews.name: Smita Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently underwent a hysterectomy at Shri Namah Healthcare under the treatment of Dr. Munjal Kapadia, and my experience has been excellent. The surgery was handled very smoothly, with no pain or complications, and I did not face any issues related to anesthesia. The hospital provided outstanding services, including a well-curated inhouse diet , attentive nursing staff, and very good housekeeping. I was able to start walking on the second day after surgery, which really boosted my confidence and recovery. With proper guidance from the doctors on post-operative care, my healing process was fast and comfortable. I was able to resume my job from home within 15 days, manage all household work by 4 weeks, and even start traveling to the office by cab. The doctors and staff were extremely patient, supportive, and always ready to answer my questions. Although the diagnostic services here are on the costlier side, I was able to manage them through my company health insurance; otherwise, it may feel expensive. However, if you choose the general ward or twin sharing package or can afford the higher medical expenses, this hospital is truly one of the best choices. I highly recommend Shri Namah Healthcare with a 5-star rating for its 5-star treatment and services. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

You are not allowed to get your food. So, if you are a patient's relative, as a local guide I would suggest don't fall for canteen food. The canteen food mostly offers biscuits and stuff like misal pav vada. 1-2 protein bars which are processed.

There is a seperate menu from which you can order food which offers options like Khichadi and dahi which are decent.
Because, when your relatives is admitted in the hospital neglecting your own health and falling for sugary oily food may not be a good option.

I would suggest they have seperate menu, which you will need to call a number and ask for, there you get better options than the processed food.

There is personalised dietician assigned to each patient. She mostly gives balanced options for the patients. I had seen Marie Biscuit in my mom's diet. I personally don't want my mom to eat biscuits with palm oil in it. So, she switched the snack.
So, if you have special preferences. You can always communicate.

One more suggestion to the hospital.
If you have a room patient's relative mostly gets assigned bed.
But if the patient is in the ICU there is no assigned bed for the patient's relative. Which is mostly offered in some other hospitals. So, that could be added.

I had trusted Shatabdi Hospital for years — my father-in-law and mother were admitted here before, and we always believed it was a reliable municipal hospital. But this time, when I went for my pregnancy check-up in my 9th month, my experience was extremely upsetting.

➡️ Doesn’t have an OT bed that can take a patient weighing 90 kg or above
➡️ Doesn’t have an anaesthetist capable of handling such patients

This is shocking — how can such a well-known BMC hospital openly say they don’t have facilities for patients over a certain weight? Does that mean only slim patients under 70 kg deserve treatment here?

I strongly feel the doctors here, many of whom seem like interns, carry their frustration and take it out on patients, which is highly unprofessional.

💔 Very bad experience. I will never suggest Shatabdi Hospital for maternity or delivery cases. If you value respect and proper treatment, please reconsider before going here

featured_reviews.name: Diago Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience.

My experience at Ramakrishna Mission Hospital was deeply unsatisfactory and alarming. For an institution associated with such a respected name, the overall standards of care, hygiene, and management are far below acceptable levels.

The trainee doctors displayed an arrogant, careless, and dismissive attitude, lacking basic empathy and professionalism. Patient concerns were often brushed aside, creating unnecessary stress and frustration.

Cleanliness is a major issue throughout the hospital. Washrooms and patient areas were unhygienic, poorly maintained, and visibly dirty, raising serious concerns about infection control and patient safety.

Despite booking and paying for a “First Class” room, the condition was horrible and unacceptable—dirty floors, stained and broken tiles, poorly maintained toilets, foul smell, and an overall neglected environment. This was misleading and completely unworthy of a first-class facility.

Time management is extremely poor. Long waiting hours, lack of communication, and no respect for patients’ time indicate weak administration and poor coordination.

The only positive aspect of this hospital experience was the professionalism and dedication of Dr. Ulhas Nadkarni and Dr. Amarish Warty. Both doctors were knowledgeable, patient, and compassionate, and they treated us with respect and genuine care. Their conduct reflects what medical professionalism should look like.

Unfortunately, apart from these two doctors, the hospital suffers from poor hygiene, unprofessional trainee behavior, misleading facilities, and inefficient management. Immediate corrective action is required.

I would not recommend this hospital unless serious improvements are made.

Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.
